controller_log_verbatim:
{"mode": "describe", "native_exit": 0, "actual_time_steps": 0}
EvidenceError: zero failed; no retry/next call

describe.note: describe returns before lattice construction, so it exercises config only.

precheck.interpretation: The process aborted itself inside the adopted 8 GiB per-process address-space cap. This is neither a wall-clock timeout nor a controller resource stop; the controller only observed a non-zero exit and stopped the batch.
precheck.failure_phase: before any collide-and-stream call; during lattice/geometry setup

initialize.reason: fail-stop after precheck; the controller never reached the third call

initial_field_read.reason: depends on initialize, which never ran

node_scaling_evidence.implication: Memory grows roughly with node count. The accepted 1.25 nm run fitted inside the same 8 GiB cap; the 0.625 nm case has exactly 8x the fluid nodes and exceeded that cap during setup. Therefore the required address space is materially above 8 GiB, plausibly in the high teens to mid twenties of GiB. The exact figure is NOT measured and must not be quoted as if it were.

what_this_does_not_prove: It does not prove the 0.625 nm case is physically wrong or numerically invalid; no physics was evaluated.
It does not give a measured peak RSS; only that 8 GiB of address space is insufficient.
It does not change any historical FAIL, any threshold, or any accepted S4 record.
It does not authorize a larger cap, a retry, performance calibration, or a formal run.

side_effect_observation.note: OpenLB creates ./tmp relative to the process working directory; the 4GiB output budget only watches the mode output directory. Next preparation must either set cwd to the output directory or extend the budget monitor.
